findings.title: Cash-dominant split payment is hard-rejected (422) by the single-tender cash guard even when perfectly balanced
findings.evidence: In multi mode the frontend builds the payload with pos_payment_method = dominantMode (largest tranche) and pos_received_amount = cashTranche.tendered (the CASH portion only): multiPatch = { pos_payment_method: dominantMode, ..., pos_received_amount: cashTranche ? cashTranche.tendered : null }. The backend cash cross-check is unconditional on split: `if ($request->pos_payment_method == PosPaymentMethod::CASH && $request->pos_received_amount !== null && (float)$request->pos_received_amount < $this->order->total) throw new InvalidArgumentException(...,422)`. Trace: total 30,00; tranche A CASH amount 20 tendered 20; tranche B CARD 10. dominant = CASH (20>10), received = 20. SplitPaymentService::validateBreakdown passes (sum 30 == total 30). canConfirmMulti passes client-side. But 20 < 30 -> 422 'Le montant reçu est inférieur au total réel'. alignCashReceivedWithQuotedTotal() cannot rescue it (returns early when received < shownTotal).
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most common real split: a party pays part in cash, the rest by card, and the cash slice happens to be the biggest. The sale is fully covered yet the cashier gets a blocking red error and CANNOT complete the order at the register — they must abandon the split and re-key as card-only or cash-only, distorting the takings. Defensible as P0 since it BLOCKS completing a valid sale; ranked P1 as a broken core flow with a workaround.
findings.reproduction: POS: add items totalling 30,00. Open payment, choose Multi. Tranche 1 = Espèces, montant 20, reçu 20. Tranche 2 = Carte, montant 10 (pick TPE). 'Reste dû' shows 0,00 and confirm is enabled. Click Confirmer -> backend returns 422, toast 'Le montant reçu (20€) est inférieur au total réel (30€)'.
findings.recommended_correction: Backend fix (OrderService.php:1071 is NOT a frozen file): skip the single-tender cash guard when payment_breakdown is present and non-empty (i.e. when $splitActive). SplitPaymentService::validateBreakdown already enforces sum >= server total per-tranche, so the legacy whole-order received>=total check is wrong for splits. Concretely: wrap the guard in `if (! $splitActive && ...)`. The frontend alternative (sending full order total as pos_received_amount) is blocked because PaymentComponent.vue is FROZEN — touching the payload build needs an owner gate, so the backend skip is the correct, scope-minimal fix.

findings.title: Z-report 'total_by_method' buckets a split order's FULL total under the dominant tender — card/cash mix is mis-attributed in the signed daily close
findings.file_line: app/Services/Fiscal/ZReportService.php:661-668 (applyOrderToTotals) reading order->pos_payment_method, which is set to the dominant tranche by PaymentComponent.vue:837
findings.evidence: ZReportService::applyOrderToTotals computes `$method = (string)($order->pos_payment_method ?: ...); $byMethod[$method] += $sign * $ttc;` using the WHOLE order total ($order->total) under the single stored pos_payment_method. For a split order, pos_payment_method was collapsed to the dominant tranche (PaymentComponent multiPatch: pos_payment_method: dominantMode). The per-tranche truth lives in order_payments (persisted by SplitPaymentService::persistTranches with correct per-mode amounts) but applyOrderToTotals never reads order_payments. Result: a 20 cash + 10 card split records 30 under CASH in the signed Z 'total_by_method'. Confirmed ReceiptDataService and Z byMethod both ignore order_payments for the method split.
findings.why_it_matters: total_by_method is part of the HMAC-signed daily Z close used for accounting/reconciliation. Mis-bucketing means the cash-vs-card split on the official daily report does not match the actual drawer cash count or the acquirer/TPE settlement — the owner's end-of-day cash reconciliation will show a phantom surplus on the dominant method and a hole on the other, every time a split is used. Cash_movements stay per-tranche-correct (drawer total is right), so this is a reporting/fidelity defect, not data loss — but it is on the signed fiscal document.
findings.reproduction: Create a split POS order (20 cash + 10 card), then close the Z for the day (php artisan or /admin via Z close). Inspect z_reports.total_by_method: the 10 card is absent and CASH shows +10 too much. Compare with SUM over order_payments.mode for the same window.
findings.recommended_correction: ZReportService is a FROZEN NF525 file — DO NOT change behavior without an owner gate / LOCK doc + triple-green regression. Recommended scope-gated fix: in applyOrderToTotals, when the order has order_payments rows, distribute $ttc across $byMethod by each tranche's amount (read order_payments.mode/amount) instead of the single dominant method; fall back to pos_payment_method when no breakdown exists. Add a regression test asserting Z total_by_method == per-tranche sums for a mixed split before touching the signed payload.

findings.title: autoBalanceTranches mis-balances with 3+ tranches — one absorber takes the whole remainder, ignoring the other tranches
findings.evidence: autoBalanceTranches computes `remainderCents = totalCents - editedAmountCents` (only subtracts the ONE edited tranche) and writes that entire remainder into a single absorber: `if (i !== absorberIndex) return {...t}; return {...t, amount: fromCents(remainderCents)}`. All OTHER tranches keep their existing amounts. Correct only for exactly 2 tranches. Trace with 3 tranches [t0=10, t1=10, t2=10], total=30, edit index 0: absorber=(0+1)%3=1 -> t1 becomes 30-10=20, t2 stays 10 => sum = 10+20+10 = 40 (overpay 10). autoBalanceFromIndex always passes the default 'auto-pair' policy; the 'last-tranche' branch has the identical single-absorber flaw.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'Équilibrer le reste' button appears as soon as there are 2+ tranches, so a cashier doing a 3-way party split who clicks it gets a silently UNBALANCED set (overpay or wrong remainder). It either blocks confirm (remaining wrong, frustrating) or, if it lands inside the 1€ overpay tolerance, books an incorrect tender breakdown. Owner explicitly flagged 'flous' / things that are not good in the logic — this is exactly one.
findings.reproduction: POS total 30,00, Multi mode. 'Diviser entre 3 personnes' -> 'Diviser à parts égales' (3 tranches of 10). Edit nothing, click 'Équilibrer le reste'. The 2nd tranche jumps to 20,00 while the 3rd stays 10,00 -> 'Reste dû'/'Couvert' now wrong (covered 40 vs total 30).
findings.recommended_correction: Fix autoBalanceTranches (helper is NOT frozen): compute remainder as total minus the sum of ALL non-absorber tranches, not just the edited one: `const othersCents = tranches.reduce((s,t,i)=> i===absorberIndex ? s : s + toCents(t.amount), 0); const newAmountCents = Math.max(0, totalCents - othersCents);`. Add a unit test for a 3-tranche balance asserting sum === total.

findings.title: Frontend canConfirm tolerates a 1-cent UNDERPAY that the backend rejects — UI says OK, server 422s
findings.evidence: canConfirm returns true when `remaining <= 1 && remaining >= -100` (remaining is totalCents - coveredCents). remaining == 1 means the tranches cover ONE CENT LESS than the total, yet the UI enables Confirm and shows 'Reste dû' rounded to ~0,01. Backend validateBreakdown rejects ANY underpay: `if ($totalCents < $serverTotalCents) throw ValidationException(...'Somme des tranches (..) < total (..)')` with zero underpay slack. So a manually-typed split that is 0,01 short passes the client gate and 422s server-side.
findings.why_it_matters: Guard mismatch: the cashier sees a green, confirmable state then gets a hard server error they cannot diagnose ('somme < total'). With splitEqually the parts are exact so this is rare, but any manual amount entry that lands 1 cent short triggers it. Inconsistent client/server contracts are precisely the kind of blur the owner wants removed.
findings.reproduction: POS total 30,00, Multi. Manually set tranche A = 14,99 cash (reçu 14,99) and tranche B = 15,00 card. Covered 29,99, remaining 0,01 -> UI enables Confirm. Click -> backend 422 'Somme des tranches (29.99 €) < total (30.00 €)'.
findings.recommended_correction: Tighten canConfirm (helper not frozen) to forbid underpay: change `remaining <= 1` to `remaining <= 0` (or strictly `<= 0`), keeping the overpay branch. Align the slack with backend (backend allows 0 underpay, up to TOLERANCE_OVERPAY=1,00 overpay). This makes the client gate a true subset of the server contract.

findings.title: Receipt does not show the multi-tender breakdown (nor cash tendered/change) — split prints as a single dominant method
findings.file_line: app/Services/Receipt/ReceiptDataService.php (no payment-mode/tendered/change rendering) + order->pos_payment_method collapsed at PaymentComponent.vue:837
findings.evidence: grep over ReceiptDataService.php for pos_payment_method / tendered / received / change / mode returns no payment-rendering hits; the service does not consume order_payments or payment_breakdown. The order itself stores only the dominant pos_payment_method. So a 20 cash + 10 card sale prints a ticket that, at best, names a single method and omits the per-tranche split, the cash amount tendered, and the change rendered.
findings.why_it_matters: For a customer who paid part cash part card, the receipt does not reflect what they actually paid on each method, and the cash tendered/change rendered is absent — poor for disputes and for the customer's own records. The legal trail is INTACT (order_payments rows + per-tranche audit_logs are persisted and HMAC-chained), so this is a receipt-fidelity gap, not fiscal data loss. Deliberately NOT ranked NF525-P0.
findings.reproduction: Complete a split POS order (cash + card), print/preview the receipt: only one payment method is implied, no per-tranche lines, no 'reçu/rendu' for the cash portion.
findings.recommended_correction: Enhance the receipt renderer (ReceiptDataService is the data layer — verify frozen status before edit) to read order->orderPayments and emit a 'Détail paiement' block: one line per tranche (mode + amount), plus reçu/rendu for cash tranches. Owner-gate if ReceiptDataService is treated as fiscal-frozen; otherwise an additive read-only enrichment with a snapshot test.

findings.title: Cash input accepts multiple decimal points / numpad '.' and '00' bypass the keypress filter — change display can be silently wrong
findings.evidence: floatNumber tests only the SINGLE new char: `let char = String.fromCharCode(e.keyCode); if (/^[.]?[0-9]*$/.test(char)) return true; else e.preventDefault();`. A second '.' keystroke is itself a valid single char, so '12.3.4' is typable. The PosV5Numpad '.' and '00' keys go through numpadInput which appends raw (`el.value += val`) and never passes through floatNumber at all. cashChange does `parseFloat(this.cashReceivedRaw)`; parseFloat('12.3.4') = 12.3 (truncates), guarded by `|| 0`, so no NaN — but the displayed 'Monnaie à rendre' is computed off a truncated value, diverging from what the cashier typed.
findings.why_it_matters: Not a money bug at persist time: the backend recomputes the order total via PricingService and validates pos_received_amount >= total, so an underpay cannot slip through. Impact is a confusing/incorrect on-screen change figure and sloppy input handling, which erodes cashier trust in the change display. Low severity, but it is a real input-validation blur.
findings.reproduction: Cash mode: type '12.3.4' in the reçu field (or tap '.' twice via the numpad), observe the change-due figure computed from 12.3 not 12.34/your intent.
findings.recommended_correction: Fix floatNumber to validate the resulting value, not the single char (e.g. reject if the field would contain >1 '.'), and route numpadInput through the same guard (reject a second '.'). Both are outside frozen zones (appService + PaymentComponent's own numpad handlers are app logic, but note PaymentComponent.vue itself is FROZEN — the safer change is in appService.floatNumber + a small guard in numpadInput, which is owner-gated since the file is frozen). If frozen scope blocks it, document as backlog.

solids.title: Integer-cents money math eliminates float drift across the whole split surface
solids.note: toCents/fromCents round-trip every amount through Math.round(x*100); splitEquallyCents distributes floor parts and lets the LAST tranche carry the remainder so sum(parts) === totalCents exactly (the 30,01 -> 10/10/10,01 case is handled). Backend mirrors this with (int)round($amount*100) in validateBreakdown. No binary-float drift in the split totals.

solids.title: CARD terminal_id is branch-scoped + ACTIVE-checked at BOTH the HTTP and service layers (anti phantom-card theft)
solids.note: Every CARD tranche must carry a terminal_id pointing to an ACTIVE payment_terminals row owned by the order's branch. BranchScope is explicitly bypassed for the lookup and branch_id is checked manually, so a forged/cross-branch terminal cannot be used to fake a card tranche while pocketing cash. Defense-in-depth: the service re-validates for non-HTTP callers.

solids.title: Split sum re-validated server-side against the SSOT total inside the create transaction (atomic)
solids.note: validateBreakdown re-checks sum >= server total (with a bounded 1€ overpay tolerance) using $order->total (server SSOT, never the client value), and persistTranches runs inside the parent DB::transaction so a malformed/short breakdown rolls back the whole order. Per-tranche audit_logs are written on the HMAC chain, and one cash_movement IN is recorded per CASH tranche.

solids.title: Robust confirm flow: strict single-flight guard, auth-retry, SSOT total-strip from payload
solids.note: Confirm button is :disabled while submitting AND the method re-checks loading.isActive (belt + suspenders); 401 triggers a single auth refresh + one retry; total/subtotal/discount are stripped from the POST so the server's PricingService recompute is the only authority. 429/409 are surfaced via the global interceptor without duplicate toasts.
